candidates.name: NumPy DLPack import/export
candidates.proposed_use: Exchange a supported CPU array between NumPy and another DLPack library without copying; request copy=False on the NumPy consumer.

citations.section: numpy.from_dlpack contract, parameters and ndarray return L97–121; example L133–140
The DLPack Protocol L109–115; Example: DLPack L277–338

candidates.opened_evidence: NumPy documents an ndarray return, copy=False rejecting necessary copies, and the __dlpack__/__dlpack_device__ protocol. Its CPU import example demonstrates producer mutation visible in the NumPy view; a reverse example exports a NumPy array to PyTorch.
candidates.remaining_adapter: Connect supported producer objects at the numerical-library boundary and respect ownership, device and mutability constraints. The complete standardized namespace remains separate.
candidates.limitations: Examples were read, not executed. Default copy=None may copy; strict no-copy use requires copy=False and exporter support. The guide describes read-only imported arrays and restrictions on exporting read-only inputs. Unsupported dtypes/layouts and all lifetime edge cases were not tested.

candidates.name: array-api-strict
candidates.proposed_use: Use the minimal NumPy-backed array namespace as a test implementation for downstream portable array operations.

citations.section: Purpose/version L13–19; strict API and array behavior L58–72; Caveats L73–80

candidates.opened_evidence: The manual specifies standard-only functions/signatures, dtype literals, restricted indexing and 0-D arrays instead of scalars.
candidates.remaining_adapter: Select and verify the frozen 2021 API edition, integrate namespace discovery, and reconcile CPU-device and production-use requirements.
candidates.limitations: Supplier targets testing, not production dependency use. Current standard edition is 2025.12; earlier editions are configurable but 2021 support was not directly checked. Device labels include simulated devices, and type-validation/conformance caveats are explicit. No full frozen-design success is claimed.
